title: Media-rights revenue for men’s UEFA club competitions set to surge past $5bn
content:
The global appeal of the Champions League is set to take annual media-rights revenues for UEFA’s men’s club competitions past the $5billion (£3.7bn) mark from 2027 onwards, a 20-per-cent increase on the current figure.

Commercial and media rights for the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League are now managed by UC3, a joint venture between UEFA and European Football Clubs (EFC), the lobby group formerly known as the European Club Association, with Relevent Football Partners acting as UC3’s sales agent.

Having already sold the media rights for the 2027-31 cycle in Europe’s five biggest markets — France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom — in November, UC3 announced deals for 19 more countries and territories in the Americas and Europe on Thursday.

These deals, which brought in a total of $910million (£670m), almost 40 per cent up on a like-for-like basis on the 2024-27 cycle, included Paramount+ taking exclusive rights to all three competitions in Canada, as well as rights to half of the Champions League games in Central America, Mexico and most of South America.

Owned by American media conglomerate Paramount Skydance, Paramount+ already has the exclusive rights to UEFA’s men’s club competitions in the United States, as well as most Champions League matches in Germany and the UK.

Led by David Ellison, the son of Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, Paramount has rapidly emerged as one of the biggest media businesses on the planet, and that was even before it agreed to buy Warner Bros Discovery for $111bn (£82bn) — a deal currently waiting regulatory approval. It has probably become UC3’s most important media partner, too.

Pay-TV service Canal+ is another big investor, having picked up exclusive rights to UEFA’s midweek action in Belgium, as well as significant packages in Austria and Poland. It had already secured the lion’s share of rights in its home market, France.

In another interesting move, American entertainment giant Disney has picked up rights for its streaming service Disney+ in Denmark and Sweden, while in Mexico and South America it will share games between Disney+ and its more traditional sports network ESPN.

UK-based sports streamer DAZN lost the rights in Canada but has picked up more games in Austria, Portugal and Switzerland, while Viaplay has retained rights in Denmark, Finland and Norway.

The upshot of these new deals is that UC3 has already locked in more than $3.8bn (£2.8bn) in annual media-rights revenues from 2027 onwards, and it still has the auctions for Asia, Middle East and North Africa and Sub-Saharan Africa regions to run.

According to sources familiar with the process, who were speaking to The Athletic anonymously to protect commercial relationships, UC3 has already reached 75 per cent of its target for the cycle, which means the $5bn target is very much in sight.

The three competitions currently bring in about $4.2billion (£3.1bn) a year, with more than 90 per cent of the total shared between the clubs that participate in the competitions.

The success of these auctions would appear to validate the decision UEFA made to create UC3, and also the decision UC3 made to replace UEFA’s long-term sales partner TEAM Marketing with Relevent in 2024. Eyebrows were raised across the industry at the time but the UC3/Relevent partnership has also delivered huge increases in sponsorship deals, too, with Anheuser-Busch InBev replacing Heineken and PepsiCo renewing its deal.

“By running such a large number of markets concurrently, UC3, together with its agency Relevent Football Partners, created a unique, highly competitive tender process that generated strong interest from a broad range of media organisations,” UC3 said in a media release.

“Once again, the global appeal and commercial strength of (UEFA’s men’s club competitions) were underlined, with multiple bidders – including Canal+, DAZN, Disney+, ESPN, Paramount+, Sky and Viaplay – selected across multiple territories, alongside a wide range of market-specific broadcasters.

“This outcome further validates the bold, new commercial strategy adopted by UC3.”
